task.description: WF-02 Step 1b hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's REQ-134 design artefact per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md's Step 1b procedure. Re-validation (rework attempt 1 of 3) after commit 2e8a570 claims to have rewritten S7.1-S7.4 as prose/assertion-contract descriptions.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary: Re-validated lib/letflow/design/req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md at commit 2e8a570 (branch feature/WF02-REQ134-20260823) from scratch -- read the artefact directly, not CODE-DESIGNER's summary, and re-ran every Step 1b check rather than trusting which ones 'already passed'. Grepped the full file for `test "`, `setup do`, `assert(`, `refute(`, and bare `assert `/`refute ` tokens: zero matches anywhere, including S7.1-S7.4, which is the section the prior FAIL was on. Read S7.1-S7.4 in full: each is now a numbered-step prose/assertion-contract description (what is provisioned, what call is made, what shape/value must hold), in the same signature-plus-prose register S4.1 (KeycloakTestClient) already used and that the prior gate held up as the correct pattern -- no compilable setup/test bodies remain, and no substantive content was dropped in the rewrite (the real-verifier override's on-entry/on-exit behavior in S7.1; the genuine-token-through-AuthPipeline + auth_context-shape check in S7.2/AC1; the tamper-then-401-under-the-real-verifier check in S7.3/AC2; and the three-count-query (0->1->1) plus user_id-equality two-call JIT check in S7.4/AC3 are all still concretely specified, not vaguer than the pre-rework version). The remaining code fences in the file (S2's one-line `ExUnit.start(exclude: [:keycloak])` diff, S3.1's `setup_all do # ... end` placeholder skeleton, S4.1's @spec/@type/prose-comment block, S5's @spec-plus-comment ensure_bpm_default_tenant!/0 sketch, S6's module skeleton with `...`) all contain declarations/type-shapes/comments only, no function bodies -- re-checked each individually rather than assuming they were unaffected by the S7 rewrite. Re-checked all five Step 1b checks from scratch, not only the one that failed last time: (a) every AC1-6 maps to a concrete design element with no TBD/deferral language -- confirmed via S10's cross-reference table and a grep for TBD/'left open'/'to be determined', the only two hits being the design explicitly declaring something IS decided, not an actual deferral; (b) function signatures fully specified -- S4.1's KeycloakTestClient carries full @spec + input/output types + prose error-branch description for ensure_started/0, discovery_reachable?/1, direct_access_token/4, and tamper_signature/1, and S5's ensure_bpm_default_tenant!/0 likewise; (c) error-handling shapes stated -- token_error() type (:http_error/:transport_error/:unexpected_response) and {:ok,_}/{:error,_} tags used throughout, discovery_reachable?/1's boolean-never-raises contract stated explicitly; (d) cross-module dependencies listed -- S1's file table plus inline references to AuthPipeline, TokenVerifier.Oidcc, Letflow.Identity/User/Tenant, TenantProvisioning, TenantFixture; (e) no implementation code present -- confirmed above, this is the check that failed last time and it now passes. Independently re-confirmed the three items named in the re-validation task: config/test.exs:85 still pins `token_verifier: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifierDouble` unconditionally (grepped directly, the design does not touch this line); the exclusion mechanism (test/test_helper.exs's ExUnit.start(exclude: [:keycloak])) applies at suite-collection time before Mix's --partitions splitting, so plain `mix test` and every scripts/test_parallel.sh partition are unaffected by Keycloak's state, and scripts/test_parallel.sh itself is not modified by this design; grepped docs/migration/decisions/ for OIDC/Keycloak-related records -- only 0002-oidc-integration.md (the oidcc-library choice) is relevant, and the design's use of Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc is consistent with, not a re-decision of, that record. No BLOCKER or MINOR issue found. All five Step 1b checks pass; verdict is PASS.

gate_history.summary: FAIL on check (e) -- 'no implementation code present (no actual .ex/.exs code blocks -- signatures and type shapes only, not bodies)'. lib/letflow/design/req134-real-keycloak-token-integration.md contains fully written ExUnit implementation code, not signatures/type shapes, in violation of WF-02 Step 1b's check 2e. Sections 7.1-7.4 each contain a complete, runnable function body -- not a signature: 7.1's `setup do ... end` block has the real Application.fetch_env!/put_env/on_exit sequence written out; 7.2's, 7.3's, and 7.4's `test "..." do ... end` blocks contain real Plug.Test.conn/3 pipelines, real Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.call/2 invocations, real Ecto.Query.from/Repo.aggregate queries with actual where-clauses and prefix bindings, and real ExUnit assert/refute statements with concrete match patterns. Other checks (a/b/c/d) did not independently fail, but per the workflow's no-partial-credit rule the verdict is FAIL on (e) alone.
